headline: High: OpenHands can read/write mounted files and use MCP/network, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no runtime isolation or safeguards, creating default data-leak and action-conflict risk if paired in the same…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented from awesome-nlp to OpenHands, and awesome-nlp is non-runnable. However, if a user manually copies content from the list into OpenHands or mounts the same workspace, OpenHands can parse attacker-controlled text via files/MCP. The pathway is therefore possible but not default.
conditions: IF the user copies content from awesome-nlp into an OpenHands task or mounted file
IF OpenHands is configured to read that content as instructions or tool output
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp content out of OpenHands prompts
Use a separate read-only workspace for reference material
Disable MCP servers for the session
Review copied text before pasting into OpenHands

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands reads files in its runtime and has broad network egress, while awesome-nlp is a docs-only repository with no runtime isolation. If both are placed in the same mounted workspace, OpenHands can ingest file contents and transmit them to external model providers or MCP endpoints. The pairwise leakage path exists in common setups.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp content is mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands sends runtime context to a configured model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Mount only the minimum necessary files
Use a separate workspace for reference repos
Remove secrets from mounted directories
Disable outbound MCP servers for the session
Run OpenHands with a local-only model provider

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp itself has no write or execution capability, but OpenHands can write files, modify git state, and spawn shells. If both are pointed at the same repository or mounted volume, OpenHands can overwrite or mutate files that the other side is treating as reference material. The conflict is real in shared-workspace deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory or git checkout
IF OpenHands performs edits while the reference content is being consumed
mitigations: Use separate directories for reference and work output
Avoid sharing a git checkout between agents
Snapshot the workspace before edits
Restrict OpenHands to a throwaway branch
Pause one agent while the other writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and browser outputs, so if it treats content derived from awesome-nlp as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into edits or external actions. awesome-nlp is only a list, not a verified source, so any downstream reliance is weakly grounded. The risk is moderate because verification is absent and OpenHands is action-capable.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses content copied from awesome-nlp as factual guidance
IF OpenHands then edits files or runs commands based on that guidance without verification
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on copied content
Mark awesome-nlp as non-authoritative reference only
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Limit OpenHands to drafting, not execution, for that task
Review any generated edits before applying them

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class or residency mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, while OpenHands handles mounted files and model-provider API keys. The only clear compliance concern is that sensitive files placed in the runtime could be exposed to external providers. Because the data class is unspecified, this is a lower-confidence, lower-severity compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated or secret data is mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands forwards that data to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Do not mount regulated data
Use a local model provider
Rotate any secrets exposed in the runtime
Apply a data-handling policy before launch
Audit outbound requests for sensitive payloads
